draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kushalnagar! Surrounded by the Kaveri river, this town is the gateway to Kodagu and its second largest town after Madikeri.
draft.hungryLine: Kushalnagar is Kodagu's busy commercial centre, so you'll find plenty of local places to eat around town.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Ganapathi Temple is a 3 minute walk, and Thaqwa Masjid is about 17 minutes on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find your way down to the Kaveri, which wraps around the town.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Kushalnagar was once its own constituency, also known as Fraserpet, and it held just one election, in 1952.

tips.title: Use it as your base.
tips.body: Kushalnagar is the gateway to Kodagu district, so it's a handy starting point.

tips.title: Dress modestly at places of worship.
tips.body: The Ganapathi Temple and Thaqwa Masjid are both close by.

story.title: The Fraserpet seat
story.body: The Kushalnagar constituency, also known as Fraserpet, held its one and only election in 1952 for the Coorg State legislature.

story.title: Joining Mysore
story.body: When states were reorganised along linguistic lines in 1956, Coorg was merged with Mysore State and the seat went with it.

story.title: Kodagu's growing town
story.body: Kushalnagar heads its own taluk, and it's the fastest developing town in Kodagu district.
